newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tells Kurds to end clash, cautions Iran, Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tells Kurds to end clash, cautions Iran, Iraq.

text.p: The United States on Monday called on the two main Kurdish groups in northern Iraq to stop fighting and urged the governments of Iraq and Iran to stay out of the conflict.
The call came as the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) pursued an offensive against the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) after capturing the major city of Sulaimaniya on Sunday.

"We are calling on both the PUK and the KDP to end the fighting," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns. "We don't believe Kurdish interests will be promoted by a continuation of fighting between them."
"We hope both Iran and Iraq will stay out of the fighting," he added.
Burns said U.S. officials had been in touch with both Kurdish groups in an attempt to make peace between them.

The KDP last month gained control of most of northern Iraq from the PUK with the aid of the Iraqi military. The group invited Iraqi forces into the Western-protected region which had been a virtual no-go area for Baghdad since 1991.

The United States responded to the Iraqi move by firing cruise missiles at military installations in southern Iraq, but was forced to abandon military, intelligence and aid operations in northern Iraq.
In an attempt to recover lost ground, the United States has invited a KDP delegation to Washington for talks this week on ways of curbing Baghdad's influence in the region.
"As far as I know that visit is still on," Burns said. The delegation has left northern Iraq and is currently in Turkey.
Iran Monday denied KDP allegations that it was backing the PUK offensive with manpower, arms and ammunition.
